Testing yourself is not how you measure learning. It is how you cause it.
Re-reading feels like progress. Recalling without the page is progress.
Spacing the same hour of study across a week beats spending it in one sitting.
A little forgetting before review is not failure. It is what makes the review work.
If it feels easy, you are probably practising what you already know.
Mixing topics feels worse and works better than finishing one before the next.
You do not know something until you can explain it without looking.
Highlighting predicts almost nothing about what you will remember.
The gap between feeling sure and being right is where most learning hides.
Sleep is part of the study session, not the thing that follows it.
Answering slowly and getting it right beats recognising it instantly.
The best time to review is just before you would have forgotten.
